title: Past Simple and Continuous: Guided Practice
summary: Use examples and support to describe what was happening and what happened next.
keyIdeas: The past continuous (was/were + -ing) describes an action in progress at a past moment.
The past simple describes completed events. They can last a short or long time: 'I lived there for ten years'.
We often use 'while' with ongoing actions and 'when' to introduce an event during another action.

activities.prompt: Complete with the correct past continuous form.
activities.explanation: With 'Omar', meaning 'he', use 'was' followed by the -ing form: 'was doing'.
activities.sentence: Yesterday at 5:00 PM, Omar ___ his homework in his bedroom.
options: did
were doing
was doing

activities.prompt: In the past continuous, we use 'were' with 'you', 'we' and 'they'.
activities.explanation: True. Use 'was' with 'I', 'he', 'she' and 'it'; use 'were' with 'you', 'we' and 'they'.

activities.prompt: Sort each verb form by tense.
activities.explanation: These affirmative past simple examples use one past form. The past continuous examples use was/were + an -ing form.

activities.prompt: Choose the past simple event during the ongoing action: Lucía was riding her bike in the park when she ___ an adorable puppy. 🐶
activities.explanation: 'Saw' is the past simple event that happens during 'was riding'.
options: saw
was seeing
sees

activities.prompt: Match each subject and action with its past continuous form.
activities.explanation: Use was with I/he/she/it and were with you/we/they, followed by the -ing form.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct past continuous form.
activities.explanation: Here, 'was reading' describes the ongoing action. 'My sister' is singular, so use 'was'.
activities.sentence: While my sister ___ a comic book, our dad cooked dinner.
options: was reading
were reading
readed

activities.prompt: Adrián was washing dishes when the lights went out. Which sentence shows that the washing was already in progress?
activities.explanation: 'Was washing' shows the action in progress; 'went out' gives the event that interrupted it.
options: I were washing the dishes when the lights went out.
I washed the dishes when the lights were going out.
I was washing the dishes when the lights went out.

activities.prompt: Put these words in order to make a correct sentence.
activities.explanation: This sentence starts with 'While' and a past continuous action, then gives a past simple event.

activities.prompt: Read the text about an eventful school morning and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The story combines actions in progress with completed events.
activities.title: An Unexpected Visitor
activities.text: Yesterday was an unusual morning at Oak Tree School. At 9:30, all the fifth-grade students were working quietly in their classroom. Martina was drawing a colourful map of the solar system, and Omar was writing a science project in his notebook. Suddenly, while the teacher, Mr Green, was explaining a difficult maths problem on the board, a small squirrel jumped through the open window! The squirrel landed right on Martina's desk. Everyone stopped working. Martina did not scream; she stayed calm and moved away slowly to give the animal space. While the pupils were waiting at a safe distance, Mr Green opened the door to the garden. The squirrel found the exit and ran outside. It was a morning nobody forgot!

questions.prompt: What was Martina doing when the squirrel jumped into the classroom?
questions.explanation: Martina was drawing a colourful map of the solar system.
options: She was eating an apple with Omar.
She was writing a science project.
She was drawing a map of the solar system.

questions.prompt: What did Martina do when the squirrel landed on her desk?
options: She screamed and chased it.
She picked it up with her hands.
She stayed calm and moved away slowly.
questions.explanation: Martina stayed calm and moved away slowly to give the animal space.

questions.prompt: What can we learn from how the class reacted to the animal?
questions.explanation: The class stayed calm and kept a safe distance while the teacher helped the squirrel leave.
options: Staying calm helps solve unexpected surprises peacefully.
You should always close all windows in autumn.
Maths lessons are more interesting with animals.

activities.prompt: Which sentence uses the past continuous for both actions happening at the same time?
activities.explanation: The requested forms are 'was studying' and 'was playing', describing two ongoing actions.
activities.hint: Look for was/were + -ing in both parts.
options: While Nerea was studying, her brother was playing the guitar.
When Nerea studied, her brother played the guitar.
Nerea was studying when her brother broke the guitar.
